content: THE Underground Raymond Bayly Trouble Maker Media Group     6 Liberty Square Suite 324   Boston, MA, 02109  800.916.8502  www.troublemakermedia.org  www.raybayly.com   DEDICATION CHAPTER  ONE Leave it to Lucas “You know despite what you may think, high school isn’t free young man, we pay a small fortune to ensure you have the privilege of an education, and it is a privilege” William Christian yelled from the kitchen of the small ranch house where he and his son resided. Lucas rolled his eyes; this was not the first time his father had given this speech. “I mean, you could have been one of those kids that had to go into the indentured internship program at thirteen and pray the company trained you in something you  could make a living off of” Lucas mouthed as his father spoke the words. He knew the speech all too well. Lucas wrapped the towel tighter around his body and wiped the condensation from the mirror, the byproduct of the extremely hot shower that he had just enjoyed.  “Molly news” Lucas stated at the mirror a small window appearing in the corner as the smart home virtual interface or “Molly” began to collate the day’s news from ANN American News Network, the state sponsored arm of the Department of Public Affairs, it was news but he figured as did most people suspected only about twenty percent truth in there reporting. “Dad, I am not abandoning school, I am just taking a year off before applying for a company sponsorship for college” the young man stated yelling towards  the kitchen, though with as small as it house was, he only had to speak softly in the small shoebox in order to be heard clearly.  They had argued this same argument since Friday as soon as he had come home that day from school and announced in all his righteous teenage indignation to his father that he wouldn’t be applying for corporate sponsorship until the first quarter of next year. He had not seen it as a big deal until his father had damn near exploded over his son’s decision.   Shaking his head and staring at himself in the mirror he put a reproachful look on and mouthed his fathers continued tirade, he didn’t need this pressure, with only a week until graduation he had too much to do , he knew dad did it because he cared, but after mom had died three years ago in a laboratory accident , his father had descended further and further into a deep depression, his only mission to protect his son, and the only thing he had succeeded in doing was pushing Lucas away.  His father hovered and was incredibly smothering at a time when Lucas needed space to grow and find out about himself and what he wanted, his father had gone from an asset to an obstacle, he hated to think of him like that, Lucas loved his father, worried about him in fact. But the old man needed to let go, soon Lucas would be out on his own and then who would his father have. Lucas worried what would become of him, but not enough to cancel his plans, he had seen in a friend of his, Simon, what happened whe n you lived to please your parents, you ended up despising them and he never wanted to despise his father, they were all each other had. Poor Simon spent most of his time trying to piss off his parents even to the point of self-destruction and Lucas had vowed to himself he would never become that person. As Lucas reflected on Simon and his escapades he glanced over to the mirror where a talking head from ANN was reporting in front of a smoking ruin of a building in some city. “Molly increase volume thirty five percent” he ordered the smart home Virtual Interface or VI for short. Instantly he could hear the mock sorrow in the reporter’s voice. “Twelve people killed in the latest bombing at a food center in Arlington Virginia today, as workers were launching the new work for food program to help feed the impo verished In the city, an unidentified woman walked into the center wearing a suicide vest” he stated with a frown to go with the mock sorrow Lucas thought, shaking his head.  Mister Walker his social economics teacher had ranted about the new program, well as much as anyone could rant against the government and not be accused of being unpatriotic and forced to report to a reeducation center he thought. It wasn’t fair, poor people worked and received a quarter food credit per hour, after like eight hours they could buy a sandwich, it sucked but it was better then nothing he thought. And now some asshole goes and blows themselves up, and for what he thought disdainfully, so they c ould be a ten second soundbite for this asshat.  Lucas swiped his hand over the playing video, it disappeared, replaced by the ten-day forecast.  He looked himself over in the mirror one last time, his father still railing about his privilege for being raised as the son of a government executive and not appreciating all the advantages that came with. Lucas rolled his eyes, first making sure his father was still in the kitchen and not able to see him he might be petulant, but he definitely wasn’t suicidal he thought. Smiling to himself in the mirror, he could appreciate the good strong chin and platinum blonde hair, the product of good genes he though t, the ocean blue eyes appraised his physique which he did daily, not out of vanity he concluded but to ensure he was normal, as with every teenager Lucas had hangups about his body and looks. At six foot eight inches tall, he towered above most of his class mates and caught the eye of most of the females at his school. He was smart enough to know they liked him, but too ignorant on the ways of women to be able to take advantage of that knowledge.  At the tender age of seventeen girls were still a mystery to him, but one he was determined to conquer. “Dad don’t worry I will apply for the sponsorship, I just need some time to find myself” he yelled to the still grumbling man in the kitchen and to get away from you for a while Lucas thought giving the mirror a guilty wince and banishing the errant thought.  He stepped from the bathroom and into the small kitchen area to find his father sitting at the table with a coffee and a tablet reading the news. The older man looked up with a disapproving glare at his son. Lucas did his best to ignore the look and made himself a simple breakfast of toast and a glass of Milk. “Besides dad, you know even with a sponsorship, I am going to have to live here for the next ten years, I mean once I am out of school, I will only be making half of what I should in order to pay back  the company for putting me through college. Stevie has it made, his dad is a VP over at Envirotech and he made enough this bonus to pay for Stevie’s whole semester. Lucas said whistfully and not without a little envie for his friend. William shook his head, noticing that his shirt had  become a bit disheveled, he quickly tucked it in around the small gut that had come with age and looked up at his son. “Im sorry, I don’t make enough to pay the costs of what they want for college, even with the raise I am ge tting later this year it won’t be enough” his father said softly, almost like an apology. Lucas shook his head “I know dad, and its not that, I was just day dreaming, you have taken great care of me, I have no complaints” Lucas said softly to his father, knowing he needed to hear that.  Before the air could grow uncomfortable from the rare sensitive moment the two men were sharing, Lucas rose from the chair putting the piece of toast in his mouth as he quickly adjusted his backpack. “I need to run, or I am going to be late” he said removing the offending piece of toast, now missing a large piece from its end. “I have my presentation today, are you going to be able to make it?” he asked his father hopefully. William smiled at his son “Wouldn’t miss it for the world buddy, ill be there” Will iam said, resolving to organize his schedule so he could attend the presentation since up until that moment of his son reminding him, he had forgotten all about it. Lucas left the house and walked towards the bus stop as he did every day. Tommy was stood at the base of his driveway looking fidgety and uncomfortable as always, Thomas Reginald fellows was a geeky overweight teen with bottlecoke glasses in a time when most eye issues could be fixed with surgery, he had been fortunate enough to have been born to this neighborhood’s leading power couple, both his mother and father were higher ups in Polyhedron, one of the four corporatations that made up the managing counci l of the New United States. It meant no one made fun of poor tommy to his face. Lucas and he had been friends since the first day of kindergarten and he smiled as he approached his friend, who looked more uncomfortable the usual. “Hey Lucas um, we should not pass the Robinsons house and take the other way to the bus stop” he said to his friend, trying to sound casual but it came across as anything but.  Lucas stopped and eyed his friend “Whats up Tommy?” he asked and Lucas had known his friend long enough to know when something was up . Tommy, deflating now that he had been discovered seemed to slump a little “My mom said they are coming to get Mrs Robinson, apparently her credit score dropped a hundred points and she is being taken in for questioning” he said looking over his shoulder towards the Robinsons small cookie cutter house, it looked the same as every other house on the block including Lucas’s. A s they stared three unmarked black vans pulled up , spilling ten soldiers in unmarked body armor. It didn’t matter that they were not wearing patches or hell even banners stating, “Black Dragon Security” Every knew who they were, they were the black ops bag men the corporation in charge of the Ministry of enforcement. The long arm of the law for the council. They watched as the soldiers stormed the house and a moment later Mrs Robins was escorted out in hand cuffs and a black bag over her head, Lucas and To mmy could hear her protesting loudly about some computer mistake, but that was all they could make out, because with Ruthless efficiently Mrs Robinson was escorted across her small lawn and shoved into one of the waiting vans, and then the vehicle quickly pulled into the street and just like that they were gone.  Lucas wasn’t stupid, he knew when Blake Dragon showed up, you were most likely going to be erased. Both kids had seen it before. One moment you existed and the next, no one  talked about you. Lucas Remembered back to Mr. Johnson, he and Mrs Johnson had been a happy couple until one day the black vans had shown up for him, the very next day Lucas had walked over to inquire about her husband, he still remembered the pained tears that ran down her face “There is no Mr. Johnson, there never has been Lucas, now please go away” she had said, the pain pouring from eyes as she quickly shut the door in her face.  Lucas didn’t know what they told you to “Make” you disappear, but whatever it was, must be scary powerfull. He thought.  It took them a few more minutes then usual to go the alternate route, up the street and then through the alley next to the convenience store on the end of the block before they made it to the designated stop. The large yellow vehicle descended from the skyroad, making its way to the landing zone. It came to settle on the ground, alarms going off and a calm voice asking everyone to clear the immediate area. Lucas had heard it so often he didn’t even register it anymore, instead lining up with the rest of the  kids and shuffling onto the bus once again, already wishing they were getting off instead.  Once the kids were settled the bus rose to the first sensor and waited to merge onto the skyway. Lucas stared out the window lost in thoughts over the argument this morning with pops, the old man was just trying to watch out for him, but dammit if he didn’t frustrate Lucas. The young platinum blonde child, for that is what Lucas still was, a child traced designs on the windows as he watched cars zip by between the sensors that made up the state’s skyway. Lucas had heard stories about asphalt roads that cut  into the towns all over the place, must have been quite the eye sores he thought. He had only ever known the skyway, looking up and seeing the constant line of vehiles snake out into the distance was comforting, knowing that things in the country were working smoothly. “Hey, are you done your report” came a distinctly female voice from behind his seat and tearing him out of his thoughts. Turning he caught the bright blue hair of Allison Thompson, friend and study partner. Lucas smiled at her giving he his f amous what me worry grin “of course, its going to be epic” he said , with more bravado then he felt. “Did you hear about Mrs Robinson?” Allison asked in a hushed tone, Even in talking about recent news there was a danger in being singled out , it had happened before where students had spread stories of things they had witnessed only to be brought into the principals office to be questioned by the authorities. It was always prudent, if you were going to talk about it , to ensure no one else heard it. Lucas j ust nodded as his eyes roved over the bus to ensure no one was paying too much attention to them. “Yeah Tommy and I watched it” he continued Sotto Voce. Allison nodded gravely and sat back in her chair. Lucas could see the event had bothered her. Mrs. Robinson had been a tutor for socio economics for a year and had single handledly helped Allison through that class. Lucas felt for her, no one like to see the reality of government paranoia wash up too close to home.  The began to descend towards the squat two story building that was the high school for his district in Arlington Virginia. Lucas could see the guards and detectors set up our front as they were every morning as the bus proceeded to land in front of the school in what was called the “insecure” section. This allowed the kids to leave the bus, make there way through the checkpoint lines and into the school or the “secure” area as it was called. It took almost  thirty minutes to pass through the checkpoints as security seemed extra tight, he hadn’t heard why and felt a bit annoyed as he hurried off to his first class, already running a bit late.  “Shit, Shit, Shit” he whispered as he approached the shut door to homeroom , he could see Mr. Garcia already at the board reviewing the schedule for today’s events, he hated being, Lucas opened the door quietly , wincing as it creaked , he could see all eyes quickly focus on him including those of the teacher “Mr Christian, glad you could make it” Mr. Garcia said annoyed over his bifocal reading glasses. Lucas smiled sheepishly and rushed to take his seat.  “Now, before I was rudely interrupted” Mr. Garcia stated with a pointed look at a very guilty looking Lucas. “Todays celebration marks the seventy fifth anniversary of New America, we will start the day with Mr. Christian and his history of New America, followed by America the Steadfast played by the highschool band, we will then have a special speaker followed by question and answers and then lunch” Mr. Garcia finished pointing at each item on the board. Lucas hadn’t been able to get past the one where he  gave the history speech, its one he had been working on for weeks and was incredibly nervous about speaking.  In front of all his friends and fellow students. Lucas could feel sweat creeping in along his forehead. “Oh, come on, I don’t need this” he thought wiping away the offending perspiration.  Mr Garcia took the class through the rest of the day and thirty minutes later they were dismissed to take their places for the celebration. Lucas reported to the auditorium. He walked in the double doors to already find Tommy setting up the holo screen with the pictures and Allison testing the audio equipment. Smiling he walked over to his friends. “How we doing?” he asked feeling a bit useless as all the big items had been or were being completed.  Allison pushed the offending blue strands of hair out of her face, her green eyes flashing a bit of annoyance at the mop on her head. “fine, the auditor should be here soon to review the presentation, she might be running late, but nothing we can do” she said shrugging at her friend.  Lucas shook his head, of course she was. Every presentation needed the approval of the government auditor before it could be broadcast to ensure that anything said could not come across as unpatriotic, to present anything that had not been approved could get you thrown in jail, or worse. “We will wait, let me know when she is here” Lucas said, making his way across the stage to thd rats’ nest of wires where his friend was cursing at the small screen in front of him. Tommy had a tablet resting against his am ple stomach as he watched the preview holo file, everyone once in a while he would tweak a wire or type something into the main computer. “What are you doing?” Lucas asked with a smile shaking his head at his large gawky friend. “The videos aren’t syncing with the timing I need, if you tried to use it now it wouldn’t que to your presentation and just look stupid” he said continuing to concentrate on the holo screen and the computer. Lucas didn’t begin to understand and trusted that Tommy, president of the A V club and geek extroidonaire would be able to get it fixed in time.  It took Tommy nearly a half hour until he was satisfied with his setup. “Are we ready man?” Lucas asked with mild annoyancve, his friend was a bit of a perfectionist and it had more then onced caused Lucas to roil with impatience. “Lucas, your needed” Allison called from the side of the stage, interrupting the conversation he was about to have. Turning he could see a short stocky man with thick glasses standing at the edge of the stage, he didn’t look happy, causing alarm bells to go off in Lucas’s head. Th is must be the auditor he thought , walking over to greet the little man. “I am Mister Snieder, you can call me sir, I am here to audit your presentation for malicious and unpatriotic content for the school” he simply stated, already Lucas not liking the little man “Okay, sir, please feel free do to so” Lucas said neutrally as he stepped aside giving the man a view of Tommy and the crack of his ass , as the young man finished cursing at a set of wires. Mister Snieder looked over disapprovingly but continued  over to here Tommy was. They began speaking quietly and Lucas focused his attention on Allison. “Not a very friendly guy, is he?” Lucas whispered illiciting a serious nod from Allison. “hey, this needs to go well, I once saw an auditor code red a presentation and the kid spent a week in interrogation because of something stupid he had put in it, so take this seriously” she hissed at him.   Lucas sobered a bit and then looked over at the man in a new light, for the first time that Lucas could remember he felt a little bit of fear and paranoia creep into his mind.  It took two agonizing hours for Mister Sneider to review the presentation and with a couple, of small notes deemed it worthy to be presented. Lucas sighed heavily as he had spent the last two hours with mental reels of special forces descending from the roof to arrest him for something he had missed in his report. Mister Snieder nodded without another word, signed something on his tablet that he transmitted to the principal and then was off, leaving the three students alone in the auditorium.  “Thirty minutes till curtain” Allison stated watching the little man walk out of the big double doors.  They spent the next half an hour watching students and teachers shuffle into the auditorium, Lucas watched the crowd intently looking for his father, who still had not shown up. “He will be here” Tommy said with conviction though Tommy’s own father was an ass and tended to miss every school activity, Lucas knew his father wouldn’t miss it for the world. “I know man, just jitters, I hate speaking in front of a crowd” he said to his friend clapping him on the back. Tommy smiled at him and then walked towards  the back of the stage presumably to ensure everything was still working smoothly Perfectionist Lucas thought shaking his head.  Looking out over the full crowd of student, teachers and parents Lucas looked again for his father and didn’t see him, the butterflies were threatening to break out of his stomach as he thought about the number of people out in the audience, squinting from the bright spotlights that now shown on him he took a breath. “Just concentrate on the presentation, don’t think about the people” he whispered to himself. The lights lowered and the spotlight descended to shine directly on him. Lucas took a moment to get his bearings, playing with the tablet as he organized his thoughts, adjusting the mic on his lapel he could hear the rustling through the speakers and winced.  He quickly mumbled an apology which illicited a quiet laugh from the audience. Lucas wiped his palms on his slacks No pressure, just my ability to graduate on the line he thought and focused his attention on the screen where the lines of text spelled out the history of New America.  “Seventy five years ago, the old United States was rife with a political body that was elected by the people, this political body was rife with corruption and dishonesty, many of those serving under this broken government were ill prepared or with no experience, the only qualification was they were able to shock there constituents enough with stories of there competitors antics that they themselves received the votes to put them in office. Worse still foreign governments with the help of a few key people de void of conscience sought to destabilize the country further by rigging elections to ensure that candidates who would do there bidding, or worse cause chaos in the already broken system rose to power.” Lucas, paused to look over the room, over the spotlight it was hard to see, but at least they weren’t boo’ing he thought.  He took a breath and continued. “These politicians propogated a broken system, passing unrealistic laws and holding yearly budgets hostage to try and coorce unrealistic campaign promises from there peers. At the end the citizens of this country realized they were the ones who suffered and just as the country was about to collapse from financial and moral ruin. The country was struck with the BioPlague. Retribution for the countries ego at trying to police the world. Over half the population was destroyed, t he broken and corrupt government of the country fled to bunkers to save themselves, sending edicts and orders that made less and less sense as those left above were forced to deal with the reality of the collapse. The country was financially destiture, people were starving, and foreign governments moved to take advantage of the power vacuum left after the collapse. And yet these government officials holed up in there protected bunkers thought themselves still in control, then within a decade the various fac tions in these bunkers began to squabble over who would lead the new government spawning the second great civil war”  Lucas took a breath and scanned the room again to see , to his surprised people leaning forward, interested in the presentation. He took a quick glance behind him to see the large two-story pictures of the devastation of the civil war as Tommy kept the pictures in sync with his speech. Lucas nodded at his friend and continued.  “Over a quarter of the survivors died fighting each other so that these twisted politicians could try and sieze power from one another. After another year the people of this country had enough.  It was at that time the corporations emerged, the four saviors of our land banded together to bring this country back to greatness.” Lucas stated, pausing for dramatic effect and eyeing the screen as the logos for the corporations appeared on the large screen.  EnviroCorp, Black Dragon LLC, Polyhedron and DynaTech the heads of these companies began to reassemble a new society from the ashes of the old one. Disbanding the old archaic democracy, disbanding the congress , they created a simple government called “The Board” run by the four heads of the companies they divided responsibilities among these four companies, taking over the remains of all other corporate entities left in the nation and organizing them the four corporations becoming the backbone of this grea t country Polyhedron organized all biotech, Pharacuetical and hospitals under the Department of Health, DynaTech took over all finance, banks and investment companies organizing them under the Department of Finance, Black Dragon took over all military, military contractor and defense contractors under the Department of Security and  EnviroCorp took over all  farms farm companies and all farmland in the country , organizing them under the Department of Agriculture.  Then the board brought to justice those who had saved themselves in the protected bunkers.” Lucas turned to see the video of the public execution of the six remaining senators of the old United States, the board made up of Roger Etheron of Envirocorp, Bruce McDermot of Black Dragon, Anna Domingez of Polyhedron and Justin Blackwell of DynaTech, the founders of there society, standing tall and proud as they dispensed justice to these icons of the old world. As soon as the video finished, applause erupted in t he room causing Lucas to smile, oh yes, he was going to pass he thought. Shooting a glance to both Allison and Tommy who shot him thumbs up.  Lucas scanned the crowd as the harsh spotlights subsided and his face fell realizing his father wasn’t there.  Tommy looked between the audience and his friend, the look on his friends face finally registering, he walked over and clapped his friend on the shoulder “he probably got busy, that’s all” he said trying to comfort Lucas.  For his part Lucas shrugged and put on a fake smile “your right” they made there bows and quickly departed the stage to an excited Allison “that was awesome” she yelled throwing her arms around both them them, giving Lucas a face full of blue hair. They talked for an hour about the possibilities of college and the score they would get on the report, once the teacher turned in the grade.  Lucas found himself alone on the street an hour later walking back to his house, Both Tommy and Allison had stayed, he had begged off, worried about his dad, it wasn’t like his father to miss anything school related and the longer he didn’t hear from him the more worried he got.  He knew something was wrong as he rounded the corner a block from his house, noticing the strobing blue lights bouncing off the houses at the end of the street. Lucas felt his blood run cold as he picked up the pace, trying in vain to see where the sirens were coming from. After two driveways he found himself in a full out run, the lights getting brighter the closer he got. As he rounded the end of the street he could see the black vans surrounding his small house with the men in black tachtical gear walked  in and out of the front door. Lucas sprinted towards the house and was almost tackled by a man in a riot helmet sporting a large shotgun “Slow down kid, where the hell do you think you are going?” he asked stepping in front of the much smaller Lucas. “Where is my dad” he asked in a near panic, trying to get a look over the other mans considerable shoulder towards the house. “Whats your name young man” the officer asked, his voice getting an air of coldness.  Lucas ignored the warning in the voice and told him his name. Before he could even blink two of the other officers were on him, slamming him to the pavement and he felt the bite as plastic cuffs were placed on his wrists “What the hell man” he huffed out , it was hard to breathe with the two men’s knees on his back. The first soldier leaned down and took a picture of him and then leaned closer still “Lucas Christian, you are under arrest for treason against the New American Government” and before he could p rotest a Blackness covered his world as someone put a hood over his head.  CHAPTER  TWO Madness Lucas awoke sometime later, testing his wrists he found he was bound to something, after shifting for a moment he could tell he was sitting, the world was still pitch black as he could feel the resistance of the cloth as he blew out a breath, okay, so I am sitting, bound to a chair with a hood on my head he thought rattling off his situation to try and calm himself. It wasn’t working, he went through any scenario in his mind where he had done anything that would warrant being arrested, his mind kept going b ack to his presentation, did the auditor flag something and not tell him? He thought, trying desperately to think back to the conversation. Nothing stood out dammit he thought trying his hardest to remember every detail of the limited encounter.  He heard the creak of a door opening and held his breath as footsteps crossed the room, they seemed to stand there forever, silent and judging as Lucas continued to hold his breath trying to mentally see through the black hood to the person who stood over him. After an eternity he could hear the scraping as chair was moved and the creak as someone sat down in it. Lucas waited, holding his breath, feeling a small bit of safety in the black hood, as if he ocould understand why there was solace in burying your  head to avoid your problems, there was a comfort in your world being reduced to what was directly right in front of you,even more so when you couldn’t even see righ tin front of you. Closing his eyes, he took a calming breath and just waited, waited to see what the other person would do. Mentally he acknoleged that Lucas was completely at there mercy, but he was also sure he had done nothing wrong and he would just have to convince them of this.  “You have been charged with state sponsored espionage, unpatriotic intent and treason against your government, do you understand these charges” the voice finally spoke, it was soft and female, not at all what he was expecting and for a moment he tried to resolve the voice with some image. “Do you understand” asked the soft feminine voice yet again. Lucas broke out of his thoughts “I.. I do, but I didn’t do anything” he quickly protested hoping his voice conveyed the truth of his words. “If you could call my  dad, he will tell you” Lucas pleaded to the unknown voice.  The unknown female was quiet for a long time after a while Lucas thought she had slipped out of the room without him knowing when she finally spoke. “We will get to that, first I need you to answer some questions” she said, her tone still soft and gently, almost friendly.  The bag was whipped off of his head causing Lucas to squint as his eyes watered from the shocking bright lights in the room. He could see a blurry figure sitting across from him and out of the corner of his eye, another figure walked over to her side of the table, Lucas’s eyes continued to water as be blinked away the slight pain as his eyes adjusted to the bright light. Things began to come into focus, and he found himself starting at a black clad raven-haired goddess.  Her green eyes were locked on him, watching as he acclimated to his surroundings there was no smile, no acknowledgment as you would get when locking eyes with a random stranger, nothing that said “I see you “just blank eyes. Looking up he focused on the large hulking brute who stood akimbo just behind here, his shiny bald head glinting the fluorescent lights giving the large man a pasty complexion. They came into focus and Lucas leaned back in his chair, trying to retreat from the pair across from him, they  were intimidating the large man just stood there glaring as the Raven-Haired woman leaned forward, trying to bridge the space between them. “Now, I need you to answer some questions and we can get through this quickly Lucas” she said softly, again with that gentle tone. The woman turned to a screen on the far wall where the logo of the Department of Security, the generic badge with two cross swords over it spun , the word Prometheus floated just below the badge, Lucas stared with interest. Pictures, posts  and videos from his home, bedroom, town and school began to populate the screen in a large grid showing him at different times in the last two days, all of them time stamped and his name floating below the image, he watched as others walked by whatever camera he was near and were also quickly identified and displayed.  As he watched two times appeared in the right-hand side of the screen in red, he stared at them for a moment and then turned towards the waiting woman. “Where were you during these two intervals?” she asked causing Lucas to look back at the screen. “How” he began but paused to swallow realizing his throat was parched, he winced as he forced himself to work up saliva and sent it down into his stomach. Lucas suddenly realized it worked about as well as pouring a glass on the hot sand of the Saraha during midd ay. “How do you have all of this” he finally got out and again looking back in shock at the screen, it was his entire life, indexed and cataloged for all to see, he never realized they had access to all of this, and he chided himself, of course they did, since security over privacy act was passed fifty years ago, they had studied that in school, the government had access to all information, anywhere.  He squinted looking at the times displayed and tried to remember where he was. The first interval was one to four in the morning, he knew that right off “I was sleeping during the first one” he said and looked back at the woman who was flipping through her tablet “You turned off your phone and your computer both during that time, according to our records you never do that” she stated as if accusing him of something and then she looked up and waited. He tried desperately to remember if he had actually done t hat, but he couldn’t’ “I don’t remember if I did or not” he said shaking his head. The large bald-headed man slammed both his hands on the table in front of Lucas causing him to jump “Don’t lie to us kid” he said in a tone just above a menacing whisper. Lucas tried to lean back further but the chair was bolted to the ground. “Im not lying, I was sleeping” he said looking back and forth at the two agents sitting across from him. “I don’t remember where I was during the second time, it was the middle of schoo l, I might have been in class” he shot out defensively. The woman just shook her head again glancing at the tablet “No, you weren’t we have six different cameras in that class and you were most definitely not in your seat” as she finished, six of the boxes enlarged, showing his empty seat in class from multiple angles and heights. At first, he couldn’t understand what he was looking at then he got it. Every electronic device that was pointed in his direction he thought everything had audio video capability  from the  holo tablets to watches to glasses , hell to some articles of clothing, and they had access to it all he thought bowing his head and trying desperately to remember. “I really don’t know” he pleaded causing the large man to glower more then he had been, if that was possible. “Your funeral kid” the woman said “This is agent Diaz, it is now eight fifteen pm and this concludes the pre trial interview with Lucas Christian, son and accomplice of William Christian” Agent Diaz turned off the screen and nod ded at the man, who lumbered over and pulling Lucas hard to his feet. He was escorted down a long hallway filled with closed metal doors until they came to one that was open. The large man thrust him inside hard and Lucas barely stopped himself before his head hit the dull grey metal wall on the far side of the six by six cell, as he turned around he watched the man sneering at him as the door closed, as soon as they had the plastic cuffs on his wrists unsnapped and fell to the floor. A small cubby hole opened in the door “Hand the cuffs out to me, slowly” said the deep voice  of the large man and Lucas did what he was told, he no sooner had handed the plastic cuffs through the hole then it slammed shut with a loud clang and the lights went out, dropping the small room into complete darkness. Lucas pushed himself, every thought turning towards his current physical state and the ticking clock until the Warden got what he wanted and Lucas was transferred downtown.  He felt the muscles burning and shooting pains as if the muscle was tearing like paper ran up his legs, but he pushed harder, he didn’t have the luxury of taking it slow. He felt a hand on his shoulder and looked up to see a middle age man with kind features leaning over the edge of the pool and looking at him “Son, don’t push that hard, you are going to hurt yourself, do the exercise set only” he said gently. Concentrating he did his best to not allow the pain to show in his face, he wanted the trainer to think all was well, and he managed to do that all the way back to the cell. Once there, he walked over to the far corner directly under the camera and curled himself into a ball, finally allowing the grimace and a hiss trying to vent the pain out of his body. He spent the first week repeating the same thing, pushing his body, hiding the pain until he could get back to that same corner in the cell, ensuring the staff were none the wiser.  At the end of the week, the pain was still there, but with the pain came recognition that he could move faster, that slowly, ever so slowly his muscles were regaining the ability to move normally again. He knew it would be a long time until he was back to where he had been, but this was progress, and progress could save his life.  At the end of week two, the pain had subsided, it became much easier to hide his discomfort and he was able to push himself further. Though he kept watch on the trainer who had more than once gotten suspicious that Lucas was doing more than he was assigned, but he never said anything, opting instead to shoot him mildly disapproving looks from time to time.  Lucas would go from session to session, between the pool and the light aerobics to working out in the yard, when he got back to his room, it was push-ups and sit ups as well as reviewing his martial training to ensure he didn’t lose his edge. If that crazy fucker was to be believed, Lucas would need it. None of this is helping thought Lucas and put it out of his mind. During his time I the rehab unit, Lucas was unaware he had turned twenty four and spent his birthday pushing himself against the impending clock. The memories of Commander Joe weren’t just fading images anymore; they were hard-wired into his synapses. He knew the layout of the mountain. He knew every ventilation shaft, every service conduit, and every failsafe. “It’s not in another state, and it’s not fifty miles away,” Lucas said, looking around the small circle of Underground fighters who had gathered at the sound of the monitors. Rolle, Emma, Victoria, and Job stood in the doorway, their expressions tense. “It’s right here. Beneath our feet. Sub-Level Four.” “That’s impossible,” Rolle argued, crossing his muscular arms. “We mapped this entire bunker with sonar pulses when we set up camp six months ago. There’s solid granite beneath the reactor deck.” “Because it’s shielded by two feet of lead-alloy acoustic dampening plates,” Lucas countered, swinging his legs over the edge of the bed and planting his boots on the floor. “Level Four was built during the late fifties as a black-budget redoubt. Joe sealed it from the inside during the coup. The seed banks, the uncompromised vaccine formulas that prove the Directorate manufactured the H1N2 virus, and the continental broadcast array—it’s all down there. And it’s keyed to my DNA.” Before anyone could answer, the fluorescent overhead lights in the bunker flickered and died. An instant later, the low-voltage red emergency runners buzzed to life, casting long, menacing shadows across the concrete walls. Through the reinforced rock of the mountain, a heavy, reverberating *THUD* shook the dust loose from the ceiling pipes. Emma’s tablet chirped frantically with shrill alert tones. She glanced at the screen, her eyes widening in sheer panic. “Oh God... Perimeter breach! Upper ventilation tunnel, Sector North!” “How did they find us?” Victoria gasped, unholstering her silenced automatic. “The data trunk,” Emma stammered, tears springing to her eyes. “When we tapped the secure archive line yesterday... the Directorate’s intrusion counter-measures must have traced the packet latency back to the mountain node. I thought I scrubbed the proxy, I swear I did!” “Doesn't matter now,” Sally said, his tone instantly shifting from maternal warmth to lethal, combat-hardened resolve. He reached behind the equipment locker and pulled out a heavy twelve-gauge tactical shotgun and bandoliers of high-explosive slug rounds. “Corporate Ironclad teams are in the house. We need to move.” Another explosion rocked the bunker, closer this time, accompanied by the distinct, rhythmic chatter of automatic weapons fire echoing through the concrete stairwells. “How long do we have?” Lucas asked, stepping to the weapons rack and picking up a short-barreled carbine, checking the magazine with the smooth, instinctive muscle memory Dyson had drilled into him on the prison yard. “At their rate of advance? Three minutes before they reach the main gallery,” Rolle said, priming two remote thermite charges. “They’ll flush this level with neurotoxin gas or flash-bangs and wipe the floor with us.” Lucas looked at his small band of resistance fighters. They were outgunned, outnumbered, and backed into a corner. But for the first time since he had been arrested in the corporate education compound, Lucas didn't feel afraid. He heard Dyson’s voice whispering in his mind: *When the enemy surrounds you, do not fight where they expect. Move where they cannot follow.* “We’re not going to the surface,” Lucas said, cocking the carbine. “We’re going to the ARC. Follow me!” CHAPTER TWENTY-SEVEN The Siege of Sub-Level 4 Smoke poured through the ventilation grates, carrying the acrid stench of cordite and burning insulation. Lucas led the group through the secondary maintenance corridors, moving in low, synchronized intervals. Ahead of them, two black-armored corporate security enforcers rounded the corner, their high-tech visor displays glowing an icy predatory blue. Their carbines were already rising to bear. Lucas didn’t hesitate. Dropping his center of gravity, he closed the distance with terrifying speed, deflecting the lead operator’s muzzle upward as a burst of suppressed rounds chewed into the concrete ceiling. Using the momentum, Lucas drove an open-palm strike directly into the enforcer's throat guard, followed by a sweeping low kick that swept the man’s legs out from under him. Before the second guard could acquire his target, Sally stepped around the bulkhead and fired from the hip. The heavy shotgun roar shattered the confines of the corridor, blowing the second enforcer backward into the blast door. “Clean!” Sally grunted, racking another shell into the chamber with a crisp metallic snap. “Down here!” Lucas pointed to an inconspicuous utility alcove marked with peeling yellow hazard stripes. Behind a tangle of rusted coolant conduits was an emergency maintenance hatch secured by a six-bolt mechanical wheel. “This leads to the old drainage sumps,” Rolle said skeptically. “It’s a dead end.” “It was a dead end fifty years ago,” Lucas said, gripping the wheel. He strained against the rusted metal, his muscles burning until the ancient gears reluctantly broke free with a loud screech. “Joe had his engineers cut an emergency bypass directly into the subterranean elevator hoistway.” The heavy circular hatch swung outward, revealing a vertical drop into absolute blackness. A rusted steel ladder descended into the depths alongside thick bundles of armored power cables. Above them, the distinct thrum of corporate quad-rotor combat drones buzzed down the hallway, accompanied by the heavy, measured boots of a full tactical assault squad. “Go! Go! Down the ladder!” Lucas ordered, covering the corridor with his carbine. Victoria and Emma scrambled into the shaft first, followed by Doc, who grumbled under her breath about her aching knees but moved with surprising agility. Job followed immediately behind her. “Rolle, plant the charges on the frame!” Lucas called out. “Already armed, kid!” Rolle slapped two magnetic thermite blocks against the heavy steel hinges of the hatch. “Ten-second delay!” Sally grabbed Lucas by the collar of his tactical jacket and bodily hauled him into the shaft just as a hail of armor-piercing rounds peppered the entrance. Rolle dropped in behind them, pulling the hatch shut. Two seconds later, the thermite charges ignited in a blinding white glare of three-thousand-degree fury, melting the steel hatch into the mountain rock and fusing the entrance forever. The team descended through the dark, guided only by the narrow beams of their weapon-mounted lights. Fifty feet down, the ladder terminated on a reinforced concrete catwalk overlooking an immense underground cavern. Before them stood the primary entrance to the Automated Redoubt Complex. It was unlike anything Lucas had ever seen. A massive vault door, forty feet in diameter, constructed of solid titanium-tungsten alloy, set flush into the subterranean bedrock. In the center of the door was a sleek biometric terminal, its green standby light blinking patiently in the gloom, powered by geothermal relays that had never stopped running. Behind them, the distant muffled thuds of corporate shaped charges began hammering through the rock ceiling above. The Directorate forces were drilling through the secondary elevator shafts. “We’re out of time, Lucas!” Emma shouted over the rumble of collapsing rock above. “They’ll be through the ceiling in two minutes!” Lucas stepped up to the terminal. The screen flickered to life as his shadow crossed its sensors. An amber prompt appeared on the black glass: *RESTRICTED FACILITY. CONTINUITY OF GOVERNMENT PROTOCOL ACTIVE. IDENTIFY OR BE TERMINATED.* Lucas swallowed hard. He placed his right palm against the cold scanner plate. A lattice of red laser light swept across his skin, reading the ridge patterns, the capillary pulse, and the deep genetic sequence of his blood. *BIOMETRIC MATCH IDENTIFIED: DESCENDANT PATTERN - WALKER LINEAGE.* *ENTER SECONDARY CIPHER.* Lucas leaned in close to the audio receiver. In his mind, he saw Joe standing at the console fifty years ago, looking out into the dark. “*Adonias has fallen. The Republic endures,*” Lucas spoke clearly. For three agonizing seconds, nothing happened. The sound of corporate breaching saws roared through the upper catwalks as concrete dust rained down upon their heads. Then, deep within the mountain, a series of colossal hydraulic locks disengaged with sounds like artillery cannons firing. A blast of pressurized, clean, conditioned air hissed out from the seal, smelling of ozone and pine. The forty-foot titanium vault door slowly recessed two feet into the bedrock and slid silently to the left, revealing the glowing interior of the ARC. “Get inside! Move!” Lucas commanded. The team sprinted across the threshold. As Lucas crossed the line, he hit the emergency cycle button on the inner console. The massive door immediately reversed course, sealing shut with a definitive, earth-shaking thud, locking the corporate strike teams out on the cold stone of the cavern. CHAPTER TWENTY-EIGHT A Voice in the Dark The Automated Redoubt Complex was pristine. While the world above had rotted under fifty years of corporate neglect, starvation, and exploitation, the ARC stood as a cathedral of lost knowledge. Fluorescent light panels illuminated automatically as the team advanced, casting brilliant white light over polished chrome floors and vaulted ceilings. To the left stood automated hydroponic bays stretching for hundreds of yards, green with nutrient-rich crops maintained by silent, solar-powered mechanical arms. To the right were refrigerated pharmaceutical synthesis chambers containing the unadulterated master genetic strains of the world's most vital crops, along with thousands of canisters of broad-spectrum antivirals. And in the center of the cavernous command room stood the Primary Broadcast Array. “Look at this,” Victoria whispered in reverence, running her fingers along the edge of a glass holographic interface. “This isn't corporate intranet. This is the old Emergency Broadcast Network. It links directly to the orbital military comsats that the Directorate could never decrypt.” Emma dropped her backpack onto a console and plugged in her portable rig with hands that shook with exhilaration. “I’m in. My God... the firewalls don't even know corporate encryption exists. It operates on legacy defense protocols. Lucas, look at the archival drive.” Lucas stood behind her as she opened the sealed historical logs Commander Joe had locked away during his final stand. There on the massive screen was the smoking gun: signed digital contracts between the founders of the four corporate directorates, classified Pentagon transfer receipts, and the  audio recording of the meeting where the H1N2 bioweapon was authorized for release onto civilian population centers. “They didn’t save us from the pandemic,” Job said, his fists trembling with rage. “They poisoned us so they could sell us the cure.” “They took away our courts, our schools, and our families, and called it 'corporate restructuring,'” Sally growled, tears streaming down his face as he stared at the names on the screen. “They murdered fifty million people to balance a ledger.” “Can we broadcast this?” Lucas asked, looking at Emma and Victoria. Emma looked up, a fierce, brilliant smile lighting up her face. “Not just broadcast it, Lucas. The ARC's transmitter is tied to every emergency receiver across the country. It will override every corporate news channel, every smart mirror, every factory loudspeaker, and every digital display in all four sectors. They cannot jam this frequency. The transmitters are built into the power grid itself.” “Set it up,” Lucas said. Doc walked over and placed a reassuring hand on Lucas’s shoulder. She handed him a small audio headset. “You’ve come a long way from that scared kid in the holding cell, Lucas.” “Dyson taught me that a war isn't won by breaking walls,” Lucas replied, putting the headset on. “It's won by waking up the people who built them.” Emma typed a final sequence into the console. A massive status bar filled across the primary screen: *CONTINENTAL OVERRIDE PRIMED. BROADCAST STATIONS: 14,892. ONLINE CHANNELS: 100%. TRANSMITTING IN THREE... TWO... ONE...* A chime sounded through the complex. The indicator light on the microphone turned steady, glowing green. Across the continent—in the crowded, smog-choked poverty tenements of Chicago, in the endless agricultural slave fields of the Midwest, in the dark assembly sweatshops of the Rust Belt, and in the gleaming glass towers of corporate executives—every screen abruptly went black. Smart mirrors in millions of homes flickered and reset. Billboard holograms over crowded city squares cut out. In their place, a crisp, high-definition image of Lucas Walker appeared, standing in the bright, uncorrupted light of the ARC, backed by the seal of a free nation. Lucas took a breath, letting his voice carry across the silent country: “My name is Lucas Walker. For fifty years, the Directorate told us that our freedom destroyed us. They told us that without their security, we would starve; that without their medicine, we would perish; that without their labor, we had no value. “They lied. “I am broadcasting to you from the Automated Redoubt Complex—a facility hidden by the men and women who gave their lives trying to protect you. What you are about to see is not propaganda. It is the unredacted truth.” Behind Lucas, the screen split, displaying the original signed corporate treason treaties, the bioweapon distribution manifests, and the video testimony of Commander Joe Walker and Major Helen Wong. “The sickness that brought our world to its knees was manufactured by the men who now rule you,” Lucas’s voice rang clear, steady, and unyielding. “The food they ration is grown on land they stole. The chains you wear are forged only by your belief that they are invincible. “They are not invincible. “Beneath this mountain lies the cure to their engineered poisons, the uncorrupted seeds of our earth, and the knowledge they tried to burn. We are coming to unlock the gates. To the guards in the watchtowers: lay down your arms. To the workers in the factories: step away from the machines. To every man, woman, and child living in the dark: look up. “The Underground is no longer beneath you. We are standing with you. Take back your world.” Lucas cut the transmission. For several seconds, the only sound in the ARC was the steady hum of the ventilation fans and the ragged breathing of the six fighters around the console. Then Emma pulled up the live satellite surveillance feeds from across the four sectors. In Sector One, the massive security gates of the central industrial labor complex swung open as thousands of workers flooded past the stunned, retreating corporate enforcers. In Sector Two, crowds filled the central plazas, tearing down corporate billboards and raising handmade banners of the resistance. The spark had caught. The fire had begun. EPILOGUE The Rising Tide Three weeks later. The morning sun broke over the Blue Ridge Mountains, washing the forested ridges in brilliant shades of gold and amber. The air was crisp, clean, and entirely free of the industrial sulfur that had choked the lower poverty sectors for two generations. Lucas stood on the concrete landing pad outside the upper blast doors of the mountain complex. He wore a simple canvas jacket and work trousers, the carbine slung casually over his shoulder. Beside him, Sally was bustling around an outdoor iron grill, wearing a yellow summer dress with matching floral ribbons in his hair, humming an old jazz tune as he flipped handmade potato cakes for the incoming refugee convoys. Doc stood nearby with a cup of real, unrationed coffee, watching the trucks arrive with a rare, genuine smile softening her weathered face. Down the mountain access road, a convoy of liberated transport trucks slowly wound its way toward the redoubt. The four corporate directorates hadn’t collapsed overnight, but their grip had been shattered. When the truth aired across the continental grid, two entire regional security divisions had mutinied, refusing orders to fire on civilian protests. Within ten days, the Directorate Board members had fled into private orbital habitats or surrendered to citizen councils. The ARC was no longer a secret vault. It was the supply hub of a reborn society. Automated medical synthesis units were already distributing vaccines to every clinic in the eastern basin, while agricultural transports carried non-hybrid seeds to independent farming co-ops across the plains. A battered civilian van pulled up to the landing pad, its engine wheezing before cutting off. The passenger door opened, and a tall, lean figure stepped down onto the gravel. Lucas froze. The man had gray hair cropped close to his scalp, deep scars along his jawline, and the unmistakable, upright bearing of a warrior who had survived the worst the world could throw at him. “Dyson,” Lucas breathed, taking three quick strides forward. The older man stopped, looking Lucas up and down with critical, assessing eyes. A slow, approving smile spread across his face—the same smile he had given Lucas in the prison cell after mastering the five rings of Musashi. “You kept your hands up,” Dyson said, his voice rough as sandpaper. “I remembered what you taught me,” Lucas replied, stepping forward and embracing the veteran. “Move where they cannot follow.” Dyson patted Lucas hard on the shoulder and looked past him at the gleaming, open doors of the mountain redoubt, where children were laughing and fresh food was being unloaded by the crate. “You did more than move, kid,” Dyson said softly, looking out over the free horizon. “You gave them a mountain to stand on.” Lucas smiled, turning to look at his reflection in the clean plate glass of the command post. Behind his own eyes, he could still see the calm, resolute gaze of Commander Joe, watching from fifty years in the past. The war for the future was just beginning, and the road ahead would be long. But as the sun climbed higher into the clear blue sky, Lucas knew that humanity would never be forced underground again.
